issues.problem: Regression from the C1-M2 fix. The new code assumes --dir is a dedicated directory, but it comes from team.checkpoint.dir, which is bank-relative and user-configurable (mb_team_ops.py:115). (a) When --dir is an ancestor of the tree, the filter at :44-47 matches every untracked path, so all untracked work is silently left out of the tar. The manifest shows files: [] and has no skipped entry. (b) When --dir is the tree root, the same happens, and :30 also writes a repo-root .gitignore containing '*' when none exists. That hides every new untracked file from git status and from mb_vcs.sh untracked, so later checkpoints and `team commit` miss new track files. :29 also chmods the tree root (or any existing shared dir passed as --dir) to 700. Both cases were reproduced in the scratchpad: an ancestor dir gave an empty tar with rc 0; a tree-root dir gave an empty tar, an empty `git status --porcelain` and mode 700. The default <bank>/backups/team is not affected.
issues.fix: In create, resolve realpath(--dir) and realpath(root). Refuse with exit 2 and write nothing when --dir equals the tree root or contains it (the parent of the tree or higher). Then the filter only ever runs for a dir strictly inside the tree, or one outside it where it matches nothing. Do the chmod 700 and the .gitignore only on a dir this call created, or one that is strictly inside the tree. Add bats tests: --dir equal to the tree root and --dir equal to the tree's parent each exit 2, nothing is written, and the untracked file still appears in `git status --porcelain`.

issues.problem: Blank-line layout of the new test code: three blank lines before `_ps` and one before the following `_wait` (test_mb_team_state.py:124 has the same single blank line before the next def). Ruff passes only because E30x is not selected.

issues.problem: The restore-hint test moves $T into $W and removes $W only on its last line, so a failed assertion leaves $W behind (teardown removes $T, i.e. only the inner tree).
issues.fix: Create W under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, or remove it in teardown.
